audit.whatIsWrong: Pop Blossom is described as a big AoE stun-and-burst with a wind-up you can react to. The single most important part of it is missing: Riot's text ends 'The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised.'
audit.why: The entire counterplay the page teaches — see the wind-up, walk out or cancel — silently stops existing whenever she is wearing an ally's model. A Wukong who does not know that will walk into it every time she is disguised and conclude the advice is wrong.
audit.corrected: Wrote the hidden-preparation caveat into the level 6 spike and gave Pop Blossom its real 600 range and 120/105/90s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The clone is attributed to the wrong slot twice — spikes[2] says 'Passive lets her clone-bait your all-in' and wants.foe[2] says 'Use passive clone to bait your commit'. The clone is Shapesplitter (W), 900 range on 16/15/14/13/12s, which she can recast to steer mid-flight. The passive, Inherent Glamour, is the disguise: she can wear an ALLY CHAMPION's appearance, and it breaks when she takes immobilizing CC, casts a damaging spell, or the disguise takes enough damage.
audit.why: These are two different bluffs and they are beaten differently. The W clone is a decoy you ignore and walk past; the passive disguise means the 'ally' walking at you may be Neeko, and the way you break it is to land your CC or force damage onto it. Also unstated: Tangle-Barbs grows LARGER, FASTER and roots LONGER after it passes through a champion or kills a unit, which is why it hits so much harder through a wave.
audit.corrected: Assigned the clone to Shapesplitter with its 16s cooldown, described Inherent Glamour as the ally-model disguise and how it breaks, and gave Tangle-Barbs its 1000 range, 12s rank-1 cooldown and the grow-on-pass-through rule. Blooming Burst given 800 range, 9s, and its re-bloom on champion hits and unit kills.
sources: enemyKit P/Q/W/E text, ranges and cooldowns

notes: The chart alignment here is Medium confidence, not High, and a human should look at it. packet.defects flags exactly this: Wukong wins 55.43% over 184 games, yet the chart the mirror committed to gives Neeko five of seven stages and Wukong none. Those two things cannot both be right. I followed the mirror because mirror-fix.js overwrites disagreement and because this page's own whys already described the mirror's chart — but if the win rate is the truth, BOTH directions need re-rating together, not this one alone. The clone/passive mix-up is the most useful correction in the file: Shapesplitter is the clone, Inherent Glamour is the ally-model disguise, and Pop Blossom's wind-up is invisible while that disguise is up. Not asserted because the data cannot settle it: whether Cyclone's knockup interrupts Pop Blossom's preparation (the mirror flagged the same gap), and whether Tangle-Barbs' root is cleansable or shortened by tenacity.
